Ryse: Son of Rome is a beautiful game that suffers from boring uninspired gameplay with little variation in enemies. You fight the same bald skinny men, and fat hairy men the entire game. If its on sale for $20 or less its worth it otherwise skip it.

I really, really appreciate the idea of casual metroidvanias, and I think Crypt Custodian is even more charming than Death's Door. It's not hard, but not trivial either, has a lot of secrets and unlocks, and making ten friends among dead animals is a very worthy quest. Some gimmicks feel a bit less inspired than others (the rafts are only used in one location, and in an uninteresting way), but overall it plays really well.

Valor Mortis has improved substantially since the 1st demo. It controls better, runs better, looks better and even sounds better. Enemy placement is different as well, giving the starting battlefield area better pacing in my opinion. The quality is definitely there and remember, this is "just" an AA game. Will update this review once I finish the whole thing, but I can recommend it so far!

I personally really enjoyed this game. The atmosphere is absolutely unreal! 

The game itself isn't scary at all, it's the constant struggle between what you want and what society wants from you that we're witnessing in the game that instills fear in you. The story’s focus on identity being stripped away through forced expectations and marriage is genuinely disturbing. Also the letters you find throughout the game slowly revealing the tragedy behind everything is cherry on top. I'm searching every single corner just for those letters and honestly it's worth it. 

The combat is ok. I hate that some parts of the map are too dark. Not every darkness is necessarily scary. but it's not that annoying. The enemy designs are creepy as hell and the little description of them from Hinako's perspective is so good. I love reading the journal.

I can definitely see the potential that would grow into Islets and Crypt Custodian here, but it's very raw and just not that fun to play. Timings for avoiding obstacles and projectiles are all way off from what would allow for smooth, skillful movement. The transformation gimmick is interesting, but not really that fun with how limited it is. The extra platforming challenges for feathers are kind of meh. I would probably give this one a miss, but the later titles by the developer are well worth your time.

Beware, this game has game breaking bugs: 
one which didn’t allow me to continue playing was a bugged save in the firefly mission, where the objective was to disable the third bomb, but I had already disabled the bomb and so I was blocked. I tried different options, and looked online: It seems other players had the same issue, and nothing seemed to work for me to unblock the game. The game doesn’t allow different save points, which could have been an easy workaround solution. 
There were also several situations where the mission objective suddenly disappeared from the map, making me retrace my steps and follow online walkthroughs to complete the mission.
Unacceptable that such a high profile game, with such positive reviews, didn’t get the proper testing and bug fixing it needs.
